Fig. $16. Controls. (A) We observe over the same timespan (100 years) two cohorts invented at different times. Again, the more recent cohort reaches 25% of its peak faster. (B) We verify that inventions have already reached their peak. We calculate the peak of each invention, and plot the distribution of these
peaks as a function of year, grouping them along the same cohorts as used in the text. In each case, the distribution falls within the bounds of the period observed (1800-2000).
